title: Development and optimization of a rapid BOD detection method using microbial immobilized particles
author: Huo, Li, et al.
materials: We used Bacillus subtilis obtained from Nantong Kaiheng Biotechnology Development Co., Ltd. Before inoculation, B. subtilis subcultures were refrigerated at 4 °C, then were inoculated into a liquid medium and incubated at 25 °C with a rotation speed of 100 r/min. All solutions used were prepared using deionized water. The liquid medium was made by dissolving a 10 g of tryptone, 5 g of yeast extract, and 10 g of sodium chloride (NaCl) together. The pH was adjusted to 7.4 with sodium hydroxide (NaOH), and the volume was topped up to 1 L. For the BOD standard solution, we dissolved 136.4 mg of glucose and 136.4 mg of glutamate (previously dried at 103 °C for 2 h, and cooled to room temperature), in 100 mL to yield a BOD of 2000 ± 160 mg/L. Lower BOD concentrations were made by diluting this standard solution with deionized water. The saline (0.8%) solution was made by dissolving 8 g NaCl in deionized water and adjusting the volume to 1 L, then sterilized in a conical flask. The electrolyte solution was made by dissolving 745 mg of potassium chloride (KCl) in deionized water and adjusting the volume to 100 mL. The phosphate buffer solution (PBS) was made by dissolving 0.68 g potassium dihydrogen phosphate (KH2PO4) and 1.49 g disodium hydrogen phosphate (Na2HPO4·12H2O) and adjusting the volume to 1 L, yielding a phosphate buffer with a concentration of 0.005 mol/L. The cross-linking solution (6% w/w) was prepared by dissolving 6 g calcium chloride (CaCl2) in deionized water and adjusting the volume to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare B. subtilis culture
steps.instruction: Refrigerate B. subtilis subcultures at 4 °C, inoculate them into liquid medium, and incubate at 25 °C with shaking at 100 r/min.

substeps.instruction: Store subcultures at 4 °C.
Inoculate subcultures into liquid medium (see Step 2).
Incubate at 25 °C, 100 r/min rotation.

steps.title: Prepare all required solutions
steps.instruction: Make the growth medium, BOD standard, saline, electrolyte, PBS, and CaCl₂ cross‑linking solution using deionized water, following the exact compositions and volumes described.

substeps.instruction: Liquid medium: dissolve 10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, and 10 g NaCl in deionized water, adjust pH to 7.4 with NaOH, and bring to 1 L.
BOD standard (2000 ± 160 mg L⁻¹): dissolve 136.4 mg glucose and 136.4 mg glutamate (pre‑dried at 103 °C for 2 h, cooled) in 100 mL deionized water; dilute with deionized water for lower BOD levels.
0.8 % saline: dissolve 8 g NaCl in deionized water, adjust volume to 1 L, sterilize in a conical flask.
Electrolyte solution: dissolve 745 mg KCl in deionized water, adjust volume to 100 mL.
Phosphate buffer (PBS, 0.005 M): dissolve 0.68 g KH₂PO₄ and 1.49 g Na₂HPO₄·12H₂O in deionized water, bring to 1 L.
Cross‑linking solution (6 % w/w CaCl₂): dissolve 6 g CaCl₂ in deionized water, adjust volume to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare immobilization mixtures for four groups
steps.instruction: Form four SA‑based formulations using the optimal concentrations identified (SA 4–6 % w/w; PVA 0.5–0.7 %; PAM 0.5–1 %; diatomite 0.8–1.2 %). Use the specific dosages listed in Table 1.

substeps.instruction: Group 1 (Control): dissolve 5 % w/w sodium alginate (SA) in deionized water.
Group 2: dissolve 5 % SA and add 0.6 % w/w polyvinyl alcohol (PVA).
Group 3: dissolve 5 % SA and add 0.8 % w/w polyacrylamide (PAM).
Group 4: dissolve 5 % SA and add 1 % w/w diatomite.
Mix each formulation thoroughly to obtain a homogeneous solution.

steps.title: Form microbial immobilized particles
steps.instruction: Combine the bacterial suspension with each immobilization mixture, then cross‑link in CaCl₂ solution to generate spherical particles of 3–5 mm diameter.

substeps.instruction: Heat each SA‑based mixture on an electric stove while stirring continuously with a glass rod.
Allow the heated mixture to cool to room temperature.
Add B. subtilis to the cooled mixture at 2 % w/v and mix thoroughly.
Place the 6 % CaCl₂ cross‑linking solution (from Step 2) in a petri dish.
Draw the bacterial‑laden mixture into a 10 mL syringe.
Slowly drip the syringe contents into the CaCl₂ solution, forming uniform spherical particles (3–5 mm).
Leave the particles in the CaCl₂ solution for 2 h to complete cross‑linking.

steps.title: Wash, store, and activate particles
steps.instruction: Rinse the cross‑linked particles, store them, and later activate before use.

substeps.instruction: Wash the particles 2–3 times with 0.8 % normal saline solution.
Store the washed particles at 4 °C for one week.
Activate the stored particles by soaking them in 0.8 % normal saline at 25 °C for 2–4 h.

steps.title: Prepare test solutions for particle selection
steps.instruction: Make glucose‑glutamic acid (GGA) solutions at 600 mg L⁻¹ and 800 mg L⁻¹ to evaluate the immobilized particles.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 600 mg L⁻¹ GGA solution using the BOD standard stock.
Prepare an 800 mg L⁻¹ GGA solution similarly.
For each concentration, set up three parallel replicates for each of the four particle groups.

steps.title: Conduct rapid BOD detection assay
steps.instruction: Incubate the test solutions with the activated particles under controlled stirring and temperature, then measure BOD with a COND probe on the rapid BOD instrument.

substeps.instruction: Place the appropriate amount of activated particles into a closed container containing the test solution.
Set electromagnetic stirring to 200 r/min with a cycle of 5 s stirring followed by 30 s rest.
Maintain the reaction temperature at 25 °C using a bottom‑mounted temperature control system.
After the prescribed reaction time (as defined by the rapid BOD instrument protocol), record BOD values using the COND probe.
